text:
Henry Cho: We need to lock what we call “supported” vs “experimental” in the public benchmark report + interactive table. PMM needs a clear taxonomy for Legal + Sales. Can we align today?

Soojin Lee: +1. For launch we need something crisp that maps to what customers can actually buy/turn on. Also want to avoid the “you cherry-picked the best region” critique.

Nikhil Sharma: From Hosted API POV, “supported” should mean GA in the Redwood model catalog + available in at least 2 regions with normal SLO/ops coverage. Anything that’s preview / limited capacity / behind support flag should be “experimental.”

Henry Cho: Cool. Proposed definitions:
- Supported (publish as primary): GA models + GA regions (docs list), standard pricing, on-call coverage, consistent capacity.
- Experimental (publish but clearly labeled + excluded from headline claims): preview models OR regions with known capacity variance.
Does that work?

Vanessa Ortiz: For regions: us-east and us-west are stable. eu-west is stable. eu-central is *mostly* stable but we’ve had a few capacity squeezes during peak (still manageable). APAC is where it gets tricky — ap-southeast is OK if we reserve, ap-northeast has more variance depending on instance type.

Jonas Weber: From benchmark integrity standpoint, I’d rather include fewer regions as “supported” and be able to rerun + reproduce. If ap-northeast requires heroics every sweep, it should be experimental (or we publish it but don’t let it drive the topline “best latency/$” narrative).

Soojin Lee: Agree. Also we need one sentence that’s defensible for the methodology page: “Supported = generally available for production workloads at time of publication” + a note that availability can change.

Lukas Meyer: EMEA lens: I’d really like eu-central included as supported if we can stand behind it. A lot of prospects will ask for Frankfurt explicitly. If we label it experimental, Sales in EMEA will have a harder time using the EU numbers.

Vanessa Ortiz: If the bar is “GA + on-call + capacity plan,” eu-central can be supported. We can do reservations for the benchmark run itself, but for real customer traffic it’s been fine with Dedicated reservations / normal autoscaling. I’d mark supported with a footnote about “capacity varies by model size.”

Henry Cho: OK, regions draft:
Supported regions for publication: us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1, eu-central-1
Experimental regions: ap-southeast-1, ap-northeast-1 (publish, but not used in headline callouts)
Objections?

Nikhil Sharma: +1. Also we should avoid listing *every* cloud region string in the report. Marketing can say “North America / Europe / APAC” and the table can show the canonical region names.

Wei Chen: For the landing page copy/tooltips, I can implement a “Supported” badge + tooltip like: “Supported regions/models are generally available and covered by standard production on-call. Experimental may have limited capacity or higher variance.” Also add: “Results reflect Redwood configuration at time of test.”

Soojin Lee: Great. Now models: I want 1) models customers actually ask for, 2) nothing that’s in private preview. Can we confirm which ones are GA in the catalog?

Nikhil Sharma: GA today (Hosted): Llama 3.1 8B, Llama 3.1 70B, Mixtral 8x7B, Qwen2.5 72B. Quantized variants exist but are not user-selectable in all tiers; we should not treat those as separate “models” publicly.

Jonas Weber: +1 on not breaking out quant profiles. In the methodology we can say Redwood uses workload-appropriate optimizations (batching/kernel selection/quantization profiles where applicable) and that configs are fixed per run manifest.

Henry Cho: Proposed model labels:
Supported models (publish as primary): Llama 3.1 8B, Llama 3.1 70B, Mixtral 8x7B, Qwen2.5 72B
Experimental models (include only if we can rerun cleanly + legal ok): any brand-new model release <2 weeks old OR anything with “preview” tag in catalog

Soojin Lee: Works. Action items:
- Henry: post final supported/experimental list in PM-812 + share w/ Legal (for claims scope)
- Vanessa/Jonas: confirm APAC region classification after next sweep dry run
- Wei: update landing page disclaimers + badge language
Let’s lock by EOD so Design doesn’t keep thrashing.

Henry Cho: Done. I’ll update the ticket + ping @Michael Grant/@Sofia Mendes once we have the exact wording.
